description:
This conceptual diagram illustrates the key geomorphological differences between Intertidal Flats and Estuaries. The diagram is divided into two panels, each representing a distinct coastal feature.

The left panel, labelled "INTERTIDAL FLATS", depicts a wide coastal area where a main channel of water (dark blue) branches extensively into numerous smaller tidal channels (lighter blue) within a broad intertidal zone (grey), bordered by land (green) and a coastline feature (yellow). A large white arrow points into the main channel from the seaward side, labelled "SEA INFLUENCE", indicating the dominant impact of tides and seawater.

The right panel, labelled "ESTUARIES", shows a body of water (dark blue) where a river (grey channel at the top) empties into a larger water body, bordered by land (green) and a coastline feature (yellow). A large white arrow points from upstream into the river, labelled "RIVER INFLUENCE", highlighting the predominant impact of freshwater flow from the river.

The diagram visually differentiates these two land cover types based on whether the primary shaping force is tidal "SEA INFLUENCE" or fluvial "RIVER INFLUENCE".
